result.title: The Old Scene Lives in the Cache: Diagnosing and Shedding Stale History in Streaming Video Generation
result.summary: Switching scenes while preserving the original subject in streaming video generation exposes a conflict: cached history helps maintain the subject but also sustains old-scene objects that should disappear. Through controlled interventions on text conditioning, denoising steps, the local window, and the attention sink, we identify how cached visual history keeps this obsolete content. When the original frames remain in the cache, KV flush and sink recomputation still leave old-scene objects in the generated videos. Replacing this history with target-scene history largely removes those objects, but also changes the subject, reducing face similarity to the pre-switch subject. We then propose Molt Forcing, a training-free method that rebuilds scene history from a cold-start target scene while selectively retaining subject tokens from the original cache. Across 16 scene families, Molt Forcing removes old-scene objects at least as reliably as an Echo-Forcing hard cut while keeping the subject much closer to its pre-switch appearance.

AI.brief_summary: 针对流式视频生成中切换场景时缓存历史既维持主体又保留旧场景物体的问题，通过干预文本条件、去噪步、局部窗口与 attention sink 定位陈旧内容的来源，并提出免训练的 Molt Forcing：用目标场景冷启动历史，仅从原缓存中保留主体 token。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对 KV 缓存、attention sink 与 token 级保留/丢弃的受控干预与「选择性保留主体 token」设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选及缓存内容对 latent 状态的影响提供可核查的诊断与操作线索。
